why: B121 (SSPN-288), the CommonJS half. `index.js` is `module.exports = require('./lib/app')`: the root module IS `lib/app`, and `lib/app` exports `{ create: build }`, so `require('..').create()` calls `lib/app.build`, never the decoy function also named `create`. `api.js` exports `{ json: require('./lib/body').json, body: require('./lib/body') }`: `api.json` is `lib/body.json` and `api.body` is the module `lib/body`. Before B121 the first made the root module opaque and the second named a value the export map could not name, so both calls were dropped. Labelled from the source.

known_gaps.why: A `require` inside `module.exports = …` is not a binding, and the front-end reads IMPORTS from `require` bindings only. The calls through it are routed (B121); the import edge is not drawn.
Same as the root module's: a `require` in an exports object is not a binding.

`api.body.text()` is a member of a member of a required module. The call walk resolves one level (`api.json`); the re-export table can follow `body` into `lib/body` (unit-tested), but no edge names `ts:api.body.text` to forward.

refusals.why: PREDICTED BEFORE SCORING (added in the #703 review). `lib/app.js` declares `create` but exports `{ create: build }`: the export called `create` is `build`. A declared function is not a CommonJS export, so the decoy must not be reached through the forward.

resolved_by_measurement: Written BEFORE the fix and scored on develop b9f0c891: `create` and `json` missed (dropped by `_drop_unlanded`); after B121 both match. `body.text` and the two exports-object IMPORTS are the known gaps above.
